title: 05. Retrieval, Hybrid & Reranking: Sparse Retrieval & Hybrid Search Foundations
summary: Covers Sparse vs Dense Retrieval, Sparse Vector Representation, VISUAL 2: Sparse vs Dense Vectors.

sections.title: 2.1 Sparse vs Dense Retrieval
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              RETRIEVAL PARADIGMS COMPARISON                 │
├────────────────┬────────────────┬───────────────────────────┤
│  Property      │ SPARSE (BM25)  │ DENSE (Embeddings)        │
├────────────────┼────────────────┼───────────────────────────┤
│ Representation │ Term vectors   │ Float vectors (768-dim)   │
│                │ mostly zeros   │ mostly non-zero values    │
│                │                │                           │
│ Example        │ [0,0,1,0,0,1,  │ [0.23,-0.41,0.88,...]    │
│                │  0,0,0,1,...]  │                           │
│                │                │                           │
│ Matches        │ Exact keywords │ Semantic meaning          │
│                │                │                           │
│ Speed          │ Very Fast ⚡   │ Slower (ANN search)       │
│                │                │                           │
│ Weakness       │ Vocabulary     │ Needs training data       │
│                │ mismatch       │                           │
│                │                │                           │
│ Strength       │ Precise,       │ Handles synonyms,         │
│                │ explainable    │ paraphrases               │
└────────────────┴────────────────┴───────────────────────────┘
```

**The Vocabulary Mismatch Problem:**
```
Query:    "automobile fuel efficiency"
Document: "car gas mileage review"

BM25  → Score: 0.0  ❌ (no matching terms!)
Dense → Score: 0.89 ✅ (same semantic meaning)
```

**The Hallucination Problem:**
```
Query:    "COVID-19 treatment protocols 2024"
Dense  → Returns semantically similar but WRONG year docs ❌
BM25   → Returns exact matches for "2024" ✅
```

> 🔑 **This is why we need HYBRID SEARCH** — combining both.

sections.title: 2.2 Sparse Vector Representation
sections.body:
```python
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
import numpy as np

# Sparse vector representation
corpus = [
    "Python machine learning",
    "Java enterprise software",
    "Python data science statistics"
]

vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer()
sparse_matrix = vectorizer.fit_transform(corpus)

print("Vocabulary:", vectorizer.get_feature_names_out())
print("\nSparse Matrix Shape:", sparse_matrix.shape)
print("\nDocument 0 Sparse Vector:")
print(sparse_matrix[0].toarray())

# Output shows mostly zeros — SPARSE!
# [0.    0.577 0.577 0.    0.    0.577 0.   ]
#  java  learn machine python science software statistics
```
